title: M4 — Can you lose a delve, and does losing it sting?
description:
M4. Gate question, from docs/ai-dm-system-design.md section 9: can you lose a delve,
and does losing it sting?

Stated as something to feel, not to measure, in the same spirit as M0. You should be
able to stand in front of a door at 5 hit points and genuinely not know whether to
open it. If you can, the loop exists.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE GENERATOR

M1's outstanding half (LayoutGenerator, ExitPlacer, world-space packing) is the other
candidate and it loses on three counts.

1. The design doc already ruled on the ordering. Section 15, Still ahead: "Prove it on
   authored rooms before generated ones, or a generator bug and a game-feel problem are
   indistinguishable."
2. M3's own carry-forward is the evidence. "Generated rooms still have nothing to find.
   PropPlacer marks nothing hidden, so reveal_prop is never offered." That is not a
   missing feature in PropPlacer, it is PropPlacer written without knowing what a room
   is for. LayoutGenerator would be written against the same unknown, and a dungeon that
   generates six rooms with nothing to find is the M1 hole multiplied by six.
3. Risk 2 in section 17 is the top live risk and generation makes it worse. "Nothing is
   scarce, so nothing is at stake... the game runs on novelty, which decays in about
   twenty minutes." More rooms is more novelty. It buys nothing against that risk.

M3 already paid most of the setup. Section 9 lists "party state is session-scoped, not
room-scoped" as the small refactor everything else depends on. GameEngine.java:73 spawns
the party once at the entrance and entities live in WorldState.entities across
crossExit, so that refactor looks done, pending the audit in the first child.

WHAT IS IN

Attrition (session-scoped party state, scarce healing, consumables as a counter map),
the Clock primitive at DELVE scale, an engine-owned objective that is takeable, an exit
that checks for it, a delve that can be lost, clickable props, DM-placed markers, a
4-5 room authored site, and more than one enemy on the board at once.

WHAT IS OUT, AND STAYS OUT

The effect interpreter and the stance layer. Section 15 puts them with the content
milestone, together, because each is a tax alone. Several skeletons in one room is N
instances of one or two stat blocks against the existing ~40-line resolveAttack. It is
not permission to open section 6.

Inventory, equipment, encumbrance. Section 16 has the re-entry condition. Consumables
are a counter map and nothing more.

The region and the watch loop. Section 16 defers them until enough sites exist that
travelling between them means something.

Meta-progression. Section 9: never. It competes with the campaign layer for the same
design space.

THE ANTI-GOAL THIS RETIRES

AGENTS.md, Anti-goals: "Do not add a third room." That was M3-scoped and it is spent.
A delve needs enough rooms for "push deeper or get out" to be a real decision. The
generator anti-goal stands until this epic closes.

ORDER

Prove it on authored rooms. The generator comes after, with a spec: the authored site
is what LayoutGenerator has to be able to produce.
acceptance_criteria:
A played session, in the real Godot client, in which the player takes the objective and
chooses between leaving with it and going deeper, and a second played session in which
the delve is lost. Both written to server/sessions/ and one copied into docs/evidence/
so it replays in the suite. Judged the way M0 and M3 were judged: an evaluation doc with
a verdict, not a metric.

title: Doors read as shut but every exit is always passable
description:
Playtest 2026-09-07, two sessions. The player could not tell whether a door was locked, unlocked, or crossable yet, and the DM answered differently every turn.

crossExit (GameEngine.java:284) gates on combat and nothing else. There is no shut, locked or barred state anywhere. Every exit is passable at all times outside a fight.

Every authored door description asserts the opposite:
- crypt door-north: 'banded in tarnished iron. It has no handle on this side.'
- gallery door-south: 'The slab door back to the crypt, shut on a dark stair-head.'

Nothing resolves the conflict for the model. waysOut() emits only '- a way out in the north wall' with no state. The use_exit schema says 'Only when the player has said they are leaving' and dm-tools.md:39 closes with 'When in doubt, do not.' So the model holds a sealed-sounding description, a bare ways-out line, and a refusal bias, and re-improvises the reconciliation every turn.

Both sessions independently invented an ATHLETICS DC 20 kick to open the door. The check adjudicated nothing: the door was open before the roll and open after. Session 2 also spent two turns trying a found copper key on a lock that does not exist.

This is fix (a): make the prompt tell the truth. Fix (b), modelling a real shut/locked exit, is filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: waysOut() states that a listed way out can be taken at any time outside a fight. Gallery door-south no longer asserts the door is shut. Crypt door-north keeps 'no handle on this side' — true of a door that still shoves open. Server suite green.
close_reason: waysOut() now states every listed exit is open, unlocked and crossable outside a fight; gallery door-south no longer says shut. Two tests lock it. Server suite green.

title: A dev-only room preview and prop-placing tool in the Godot editor
description:
Placing props by typing x/y into room JSON, restarting the server and walking to the room
is the loop that authoring 4-5 rooms with 20+ props each would run several hundred times.
A dev-only Godot editor tool collapses it: load a room, see it with the real meshes, drag
a prop to a square, write the position back.

It also happens to be where the appearance work in 4h9.7 gets done. Choosing which of
eleven container meshes reads right in a torchlit crypt is a judgement made by looking,
and in the tool it is a dropdown rather than an edit-restart-walk cycle.

WHAT MAKES THIS CHEAP HERE

room.gd contains no reference to Table - its own docstring says so, "this node reads
nothing from Table, so both go through one build path". And room.gd:554 _to_world already
falls back to a self-centred grid when there is no World ancestor. A Room node standing
alone in an editor scene builds itself correctly. That fallback exists for another reason
(an unregistered room draws on the entrance rather than at NaN) but it is what makes the
preview a small script rather than a port.

Room.build reads eight keys: roomId, width, height, floorType, wallType, lighting, exits,
coveredWalls, plus visited via level_for.

Props are not built by Room. world.gd:236 _instance_prop does it, reading id, hidden,
type, x, y, rotation, and calling configure(prop, room_id) - which mesh_prop.gd:32 does
without touching Table either. So props are editor-safe too.

TWO RULES THAT DECIDE WHETHER THIS IS AN ASSET OR A LIABILITY

Extract the prop instancing into one shared function that world.gd and the tool both
call. Do not copy it. _rebuild_rooms already makes this argument about rooms: "One build
path for all of them (Room.build), so the wall rule cannot come out differently on either
side of a door." The tool is a third caller. A preview that builds props its own way is a
preview that lies.

Round-trip the whole JSON file on write. Parse it, mutate only the x, y and rotation of
the prop that moved, re-serialize. Never rebuild the file from the fields the tool knows
about - that silently drops description, contains, hidden and revealHint, and the loss
does not show up until a session plays wrong.

THE SOURCE OF TRUTH DOES NOT MOVE

Room JSON stays the definition; the tool is an editor for it and never a second place a
room is defined. Same reasoning as invariant 8, applied to content instead of state.

For a single room the content shape is close enough to the wire shape to read directly:
crypt.json already carries roomId, width, height, floorType, wallType, lighting, props
and exits at the top level, and its exits already carry x, y and direction. Add
visited=true and coveredWalls=[] and Room.build accepts it - and for a lone room the empty
coveredWalls is correct rather than a shortcut, per scene_fixtures.gd: "A lone room is
nearest the entrance by definition and so covers nothing."

That stops being true the moment you want to preview two rooms side by side, because
coveredWalls is then a real answer only Rooms.coveredWalls() can give. At that point add a
server flag - dump the actual RoomView JSON next to what RoomDumper already writes - and
have the tool eat the wire shape. Do not reimplement coveredWalls in GDScript; it took
three attempts server-side and the failures were holes in walls.

PATHS

Room JSON lives at server/src/main/resources/content/rooms/, outside res:// (which is
godot/). Reach it with ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://") plus a relative hop, not a
hardcoded absolute path and not a symlink, so it survives the repo being cloned elsewhere.
Gradle copies resources at build; a running server picks up an edit on restart.
acceptance_criteria:
A dev-only editor tool loads a room from its JSON, renders it with the real kit meshes and
the game's own build path, and writes a moved prop's x, y and rotation back to the source
file with every other field preserved byte for byte. Prop instancing is one function that
the game and the tool share. Nothing in the tool is on the shipped path.
notes:
SPIKE RUN 2026-09-07, and what it settled. godot/dev/preview_room.gd is on disk and works:
the crypt draws in the editor viewport with the real kit meshes - 144 floor, 48 walls,
16 torches, 7 of 8 props, the eighth being door-north (DOOR), which is correct because
the door is the wall segment. It is a prototype, not this issue's deliverable: read-only,
single-room, and carrying three copies of code the real tool must share instead.

THE RULE THE SPIKE COST FOUR ROUND TRIPS TO LEARN

A non-@tool script is a PLACEHOLDER INSTANCE in the editor. It keeps its exported values
and loses every method. So anything editor tooling needs to CALL needs @tool; anything it
merely instantiates from code (Room) does not. The symptom is always the same line -
"Attempt to call a method on a placeholder instance" - and it is worth recognising on
sight, because it names the wrong file: it names the caller.

Now @tool, and all four are permanent rather than spike-only:

  world/prop_table.gd     - scene_for() could not be called, so no prop drew at all
  world/props/mesh_prop.gd - configure() builds PILLAR and RUBBLE meshes at runtime
  world/props/sarcophagus.gd - _ready() mounts the lid skull
  world/props/alcove.gd   - _ready() positions the recess pieces

The last two carry an _editing_myself() guard and need it. Their _ready writes to
transforms that belong to the .tscn, so a bare @tool would bake computed positions into
the authored file the next time someone opened and saved alcove.tscn. The guard is
`Engine.is_editor_hint() and get_tree().edited_scene_root == self` - skip when this node
IS the scene being edited, run when it is an instance built somewhere else, which is all
the preview ever makes.

world/world.gd MUST NOT get @tool. Its _ready connects to the Table autoload, so an
editor-resident World is a live websocket client inside the editor. Everything the tool
wants from World - grid_to_world, room_origin - has to come from somewhere else.

TWO TRAPS WITH NO ERROR MESSAGE BETWEEN THEM

Adding @tool to a script does not take effect in a running editor. The placeholder stays
loaded and the same error repeats, which reads exactly like the edit not working.
Project > Reload Current Project after any @tool change.

Do not open world.tscn to host the preview. Its root IS a World, Room._host_world walks
up the tree and finds it, and every call through it fails on the placeholder
(room.gd:551 room_origin, room.gd:558 grid_to_world). preview_room.gd now refuses that
case by name. A blank 3D scene plus its own WorldEnvironment is the arrangement that
works.

ONE MORE FOR WHOEVER IS LOOKING AT PROPS

The editor's Preview Sun and Preview Environment toggles are on by default and stack on
top of whatever environment the tool adds, so the room reads far brighter than the game.
Turn both off before judging how a mesh looks, or every appearance decision in 4h9.7 gets
made under the wrong light.

WHAT THE REAL TOOL STILL HAS TO DO

Write back (the whole point, and absent). Share the prop instancing with world.gd instead
of copying it. Share grid_to_world instead of copying it. Read the environment off
world.tscn instead of restating its four numbers. Handle more than one room, which is
where the --dump-view server flag becomes necessary because coveredWalls stops being [].
Pick the room from a list rather than a const you edit and re-run.

Unrelated and pre-existing, so nobody chases it twice: the three "Unicode parsing error /
Unexpected NUL character" lines at editor startup are addons/gut/source_code_pro.fnt, a
binary bitmap font Godot tries to read as UTF-8. Committed in 47fae7f, untouched. Every
text file in the project is clean UTF-8 with no NUL bytes.

title: Combat verbs and initiative live in the frame, only during a fight
description:
combat_bar.gd is a 42px strip pinned to the top of the overlay. Relocate its
contents into the frame: initiative chips along the top of the playfield (over
the world, like the party badge), and Attack / Move / End Turn in the chin,
right of the log.

These exist only while Table.mode is COMBAT (and while the existing bar would
have been visible, including the dissolve). Exploration has no chips and no
verbs; the log takes the chin width.

End Turn keeps Net.end_turn(activeId). Attack and Move do not grow new click
modes — they are visible verbs for click-the-board, dimmed from
actionAvailable / movementRemaining the way the current bar already does.

Reuse combat_bar.gd timing (arrival(), CHIP_* constants, backdating from
opened_at) so a mid-fight reconnect does not replay the drums. Layout changes;
the ceremony does not.
design:
The 42px CombatBar Control can move or the script can be hung on new nodes in
the frame. Do not duplicate the fold of CombatView. Debug → start combat is
the play path.

The old top strip going away is the point: mode is legible from whether chips
and verbs exist, not from a bar across the sky.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exploration: no initiative chips, no Attack/Move/End Turn.
- Debug → start combat: chips appear over the playfield, verbs appear in the chin, End Turn still ends the turn.
- Movement remaining and action available still gate the verbs from the server's CombatView.
- Arrival timing still uses opened_at / arrival() so a reconnect does not restage the ceremony.
- Existing combat_bar tests updated for the new nodes and still pass.
close_reason: Chips over the playfield, Attack/Move/End Turn in the chin, only during a fight (including dissolve). CombatView still gates the verbs; arrival() timing unchanged; End Turn still Net.end_turn.

title: Dramatic rolls take the chin as a free-standing die
description:
dice_tray.gd is a bottom-right overlay Control drawing tumble.gd samples. Move
that presentation into the chin's right side. The die is free-standing — no
inner tray well, no recessed pit. Stakes, arithmetic, and outcome sit around it
(ATHLETICS CHECK · DC 20, 14 + 3 = 17, HIT/SUCCESS) the way the tray already
does from the first frame.

Visible only while a dramatic roll is in flight (Tumble.is_dramatic: attacks,
checks, saves). Damage and initiative stay log-only. When nothing is in flight
the chin-right is empty (or occupied only by combat verbs if a fight is open).

A check during exploration shows the die without Attack/Move/End Turn. An
attack during combat can show the die next to the verbs. No full-screen check
overlay in this task.

tumble.gd stays pure and stays the only thing that decides where a sample is.
Clock.hold timing is unchanged. No click-to-throw.
design:
Keep DiceTray as overlay chrome, not a 3D object in World (test_chrome already
pins that). Re-anchor it into the chin. COMBAT_HOLD_MS, land_at, reveal_at,
IMPACT_BEAT_MS stay.

The log already records the same roll; the chin die is the ritual, the log is
the record. They must not drift — caption() is shared.
acceptance_criteria:
- No die in the chin when no dramatic roll is in flight.
- debug → roll d20 (or a skill check) shows a free-standing d20 in the chin with stakes and 14 + 3 = 17-style arithmetic around it, not inside a tray well.
- Exploration check: die appears, combat verbs do not.
- Combat attack: die may appear beside the verbs; tray dismissal on the swing is unchanged.
- tumble.gd is not rewritten. dice_tray and chrome tests pass.

title: Float the party badge over the playfield

Subscribe to Table.scene_changed (and hp diffs already folded into scene). The
badge owns no facts. Green is yours (#7fae56), matching combat_bar.gd.

Mouse filter ignore on the badge so it cannot swallow a click meant for the
board — same lesson as brazier-east shadowing the door.

- No left character column. The crypt is full playfield width.
- A circular badge over the playfield shows Roderick, HP 12/12, AC 16 from a local table.

title: Inset WorldView in a stone frame and move the log into the chin
description:

Do not overlay the chin on a full-window world. If WorldView stays full-window
the camera centres on the window and the near edge of the room sits under the
chin — that is the failure the old spec §9 warned about, solved here by making
the SubViewport the playfield.

Proportions are of the window, judged in the editor against the D3 mockups, not
the 12.5%/21% numbers in the 2026-08-22 spec.

Files: godot/chrome/chrome.tscn, chrome.gd if forwarding needs a tweak,
godot/test/test_chrome.gd (the 1:1 window-size and log-veil assertions).
acceptance_criteria:
- WorldView no longer fills the window; SubViewport size matches the playfield Control, not the window.
- The log and 'What do you do?' sit in the chin below the crypt, not as a veil over it.
- test_the_project_boots_into_chrome_with_an_empty_stretching_world is updated and passes.

- Room name is visible on the lintel.

title: More than one hostile on the board
description:
"Several skeletons in one room." Today the board holds one goblin and GoblinAi runs it.

WHAT IS IN

More than one hostile alive at once, in initiative, each taking a turn. A second stat
block so a fight has composition rather than a stack of one thing - the Skeleton_Warrior
mesh is already the goblin's, so this is content and turn order, not art.

Authored spawns. M3 carried this forward: "Authored secrets still have no spawn.
Listening at the lid produced a durable fact and no goblin. theSarcophagus says Vessk is
in the box; spawn_entity is still a model decision. The hotdog class, now behind a door."
A room that says something is in the sarcophagus should be able to put it there without
the model choosing to.

WHAT IS OUT, AND THIS IS THE LINE THAT MATTERS

Not the effect interpreter. Not conditions, resistances, reach, cover, opportunity
attacks. Section 15 puts the SRD engine, the content and the stance layer in one
milestone together, after this one, because each is a tax alone: "an effect interpreter
with a single attack to interpret, or a stance call choosing between aggressive and
aggressive, is overhead."

N enemies against the existing forty lines of resolveAttack is the whole scope. If this
task starts modelling conditions, it has gone wrong.

Not the stance layer either. Section 16's re-entry condition is "a second monster kind
exists, so there is a choice to make and a fight can read as coordinated" - which this
task creates. Note it when it lands; do not build it here.

WATCH THE NARRATION BUDGET

One narration call per enemy turn, move and swing together, is the existing rule and it
exists to stop combat going to a five-second-per-click clock. With four hostiles that
rule is load-bearing rather than a nicety. AGENTS.md, Combat narration, and the open
"attacking during an enemy-turn narration drops the kill's narration" defect both get
worse with more enemies - decide whether the board locks or the beat queues before
finding out at four skeletons.

Initiative currently throws one roll at a time in the tray. Every combatant at once is
why initiative is not dramatic; check that holds at N.
acceptance_criteria:
A fight with at least three hostiles of two kinds resolves end to end with no model in
the path, under debug start combat. Room content can spawn a hostile without the model
calling spawn_entity. resolveAttack is unchanged in shape. One narration call per enemy
turn still holds, and a full enemy round stays inside the four-second budget.

title: Author the site - 4-5 rooms, an objective, a way out
description:
Retires the AGENTS.md anti-goal "do not add a third room". That was M3-scoped and it is
spent: two rooms cannot hold a decision about whether to push deeper.

Section 9, Bounded sites: "Sites are finite: a handful of rooms, an objective, an exit,
an ending. Quest-linked, scattered across the region, many of them. Not a hole that
generates downward forever."

SHAPE

Four or five rooms. An entrance that is also the way out. Two middles. A room holding
the objective, sitting shallow. Something worth taking that sits deeper than the
objective does - that is the greed decision, and section 9 calls it "tension for free,
inside a bounded space, with an ending".

The crypt and the gallery are the fixed points every M0 through M3 measurement was taken
in. Extend the site around them rather than replacing them, or the comparison is gone.

WHY THIS IS ALSO THE GENERATOR SPEC

M1's outstanding half comes after this epic, and the reason it comes after is that
nobody yet knows what a generated room has to contain. M3 carried the symptom forward:
"Generated rooms still have nothing to find. PropPlacer marks nothing hidden, so
reveal_prop is never offered."

Authoring the site answers it. Whatever these rooms need - a hidden prop, an encounter
slot, an objective anchor, a place for a clock to tick, a way out - is what
LayoutGenerator and PropPlacer have to be able to produce. Write that list down as it
emerges; it is the input to the next milestone.

TWO THINGS THE 2026-09-07 PLAYTEST SAYS TO GET RIGHT

Door descriptions must match what crossExit actually enforces. Both sessions invented an
ATHLETICS DC 20 to kick a door that was never shut, because every authored door said
"no handle on this side" while the engine refused nothing but leaving mid-fight. If a
door in this site is meant to be shut, it needs emberdelve-ql3 behind it. If it is not,
its description must not say so.

Put revealHints where a player will actually look. The gallery niche was never found in
either session - its hint is on the west wall and both players searched the brazier and
the pillars.
acceptance_criteria:
Four or five authored rooms forming one site with an entrance that is also the exit, an
objective placed shallow, and something worth more placed deeper. Every door description
agrees with what the engine enforces. A written list of what a room in this site must be
able to contain, as the generator milestone's input.

title: Spend the kits - a prop appearance layer, not forty more PropTypes
description:
The kits on disk hold 145 GLBs - dungeon_props 48, ruins 92, characters 5. The game
uses six PropType values and ships five client scenes (DOOR came out of prop_table.tres
at the M3 playtest, because the wall hangs the door). Barrels, crates, chests, pots,
bookcases, tables, statues, cobwebs, skulls, banners, candles, bear traps, trapdoors and
spikes are all sitting there unused. The 4-5 room site is the reason to spend them.

THE TRAP TO AVOID

PropType is the enum ToolSchema builds the model's tool definitions from. Growing it
from six values to forty grows every schema the model reads every turn and hands it
forty things to hallucinate - and AGENTS.md already records that the tools model
hallucinates props. Section 9 says the way out: "props are handles, not depictions...
One generic container mesh does an enormous amount of work that way."

PROPOSED SHAPE - overrule this if you disagree, but decide it before authoring rooms

Separate what a prop MEANS from what it LOOKS LIKE.

  PropType stays small and mechanical. It answers: does this block a square, is it a
  container, is it a light source, is it a recess in a wall, is it scenery. Roughly
  today's six plus CONTAINER, STATUE, FURNITURE, REMAINS and a scenery catch-all.

  A new closed appearance field per type picks the mesh. CONTAINER covers Chest,
  Chest_Gold, Barrel, Barrel2, Crate, Pot1, Pot2, Pot3, Bag_Standing, Vase and Bucket -
  one type, eleven looks. STATUE covers Fox, Horse and Stag.

The tool schema names the type. reveal_prop and clicking both address props by id
anyway, so schema width stops growing with the kit while the room stops looking the same
twice.

THREE RULES THAT FALL OUT OF THAT

Appearance must never change blocking. PropType.blocksMovement is derived from the type
on purpose - the comment says a per-prop flag "would only be a chance to disagree with
the mesh". A CONTAINER blocks whether it is a chest or a barrel, or that reasoning is
gone.

The DM reads description, not the mesh name. The prop description field already carries
the specific look in prose. Appearance is a renderer concern and the seam is already
there.

The server ships appearance, the client never picks it (invariant 1). A client that
chose its own mesh would render a replayed session differently from the session.

THE PICKING HAZARD, AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL

From the 2026-09-06 playtest: "Only things you can act on are pick targets"... brazier-east,
"a 1x1 box around a narrow bowl, standing between the camera corner and the north wall -
won the ray, had no intent to offer, and fell through to a square that was null because
the ray had already left the room. The click did nothing and the failure was silent."

A room with twenty-five props is exactly where that comes back. Scenery must not shadow
a handle. And "a one-prop fixture will not find a picking bug" - test_overlay.gd's
DOORWAY fixture carries the crypt's furniture today and needs to carry a dense room.

HOUSEKEEPING

kits/crypt.json is the only kit manifest. ruins/ is an overgrown outdoor palette and is
most of where room-to-room variety will actually come from - a second manifest is
probably part of this.

kits/kaykit_dungeon/ and kits/kaykit_halloween/ hold zero GLBs. Find out whether they
are empty or unimported before assuming the inventory is 145.

Each kit keeps its own folder. Kit GLBs reference textures by relative path and mixing
two kits in one directory silently paints one with the other atlas (AGENTS.md,
Characters). ruins/ and dungeon_props/ are already separate; keep it that way.

Adding props is not a licence to retune lighting. The anti-goal timeboxes that and
emberdelve-27l already holds the one open lighting question.
acceptance_criteria:
A room renders around twenty props drawn from at least two kits and does not read as the
same room twice. The model's tool schema is no wider than it is today. Blocking is still
derived from PropType alone. test_overlay.gd holds a densely furnished room and turns red
if a scenery prop shadows the door or any other handle.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-09-07: the inventory figures in the description undercount. The original survey searched *.glb only, and two kits ship *.gltf. Real totals: dungeon_props 48 glb, ruins 92 glb, kaykit_dungeon 26 gltf, kaykit_halloween 15 gltf, characters 5 glb - 186 mesh files, not 145. kaykit_dungeon is not empty; it is the kit already in use, and room.gd names its floors, walls and torches directly. kaykit_halloween is 15 unused meshes and it is the most on-theme set on disk for this site: coffin, coffin_decorated, crypt, shrine, shrine_candles, plaque, plaque_candles, arch_gate, lantern_standing, pillar, skull, ribcage, bone_A/B/C. Note lantern_standing in particular - the 2026-09-06 playtest recorded that invented lanterns travel with the party as facts with no prop behind them, and there is a mesh for one.

title: A delve can end - extracted, empty-handed, or lost
description:
The gate is "does losing it sting", so a delve has to be losable and the loss has to
land. Section 9: "A delve can be lost, and losing it costs the run rather than a click."

Three endings at least: extracted with the objective, extracted without it, and lost.
Lost is a party wipe today because the party is one member; the shape should not assume
that.

There is prior art in this repo for the moment itself. From AGENTS.md, Since fixed:
"A dead player character used to be only a dropped token. Combat ended, the mode pill
flipped back to EXPLORATION, and nothing said what had happened - with the input box
refusing text and the board refusing clicks, that reads as a crash rather than a death."
The React Defeat screen solved it by marking the moment and offering the way on. That
screen predates the Godot migration; check what survived it. Either way the delve ending
needs the same treatment and more of it, because now there is a run to have lost rather
than a session to restart.

What makes it sting is what was spent, so the ending should say it: rooms entered,
potions drunk, what was carried, what was left behind. That is a read of state, not a
narration call, though a narration call over it is cheap and probably right.
acceptance_criteria:
Three endings reachable and distinguishable, each ending the delve as a state rather
than a screen. The client shows what was spent and what was carried out. Restarting is
one action and does not need the terminal.

title: The objective is an engine-owned prop, and the exit checks for it
description:
Section 9, Props are handles: "The objective is engine-owned, never narrator-asserted.
It is a prop with an id, taking it emits an event, and the exit checks for it. This is
the difference between an objective and a copper key."

The copper key is the reference failure and it is worth restating because this task is
the fix for it. The M2 gate produced a copper key found in a lamp's fat, asserted,
durable, and turning a lock in a door that still could not open (m2-evaluation.md
section 4). assert_fact made the DM consistent about it; nothing made the board agree.
An objective that lives in facts is another copper key. This one is a Prop with an id,
a take event, and a fold.

Depends on props being click targets. Routing "take the relic" through free text alone
puts a mechanical outcome back on the narrator's side of the governing principle —
section 2a says exactly this, and it is why the exits-only rule was reversed.

Section 9 also says where it sits: "the objective sits shallow and there is more worth
taking deeper, so the player can leave the moment they have what they came for. That is
tension for free, inside a bounded space, with an ending."

The exit checking for it is half the task. Leaving without the objective is legal and
means something different from leaving with it.
acceptance_criteria:
The objective is a Prop with an id in room content. Taking it emits an event that folds
into WorldState. The exit reads that state. A test takes it, leaves, and asserts the
delve ended carrying it; a second test leaves without it and asserts a different ending.
No fact and no narration is load-bearing in either path.

title: The Clock primitive, at DELVE scale
description:
Section 9, The delve clock: "Without pressure, go deeper costs nothing and the greed
decision is fake. A clock is the pressure."

Build the primitive from section 9 exactly, at DELVE scale only:

  record Clock(ClockId id, ClockScale scale, int filled, int segments,
               ClockKind kind, ConsequenceId consequence)

Three scales are named in the design (DELVE, WATCH, FRONT) and only DELVE is in scope.
The enum carries all three because the record is meant to be built once — section 9,
One primitive, three scales. Do not build the other two.

Ticks on rooms entered, rests taken, and noisy failures. When it fills it fires a table.
The table is the point: it is the same constrain-the-model pattern as the DC bands in
section 7 and the prop enum in section 5. The DM narrates what the table produced; it
never decides that the torch went out.

Consequences reach the prompt through the world-state projection (section 12), which
never truncates, so a filling clock is something the DM can foreshadow honestly. That is
the same reason the projection works at all: the DM cannot contradict a board that is in
front of it.
acceptance_criteria:
A Clock record with a tick event and a fold. At least two clocks running in a delve —
light and one of alert or wandering. Filling one fires a consequence from a table, not
from the model. The DM prompt shows clock state every turn. A scripted test fills a clock
and asserts the consequence, with no model in the path.

title: Consumables as a counter map, and one use_item tool
description:
Section 9, Attrition: "Consumables are a counter map, not an inventory.
Map<Consumable, Integer> on PartyMember over a closed enum — potion, torch, rope — and
one use_item tool. No item entities, no equipping, no weight, no UI beyond a count."

The reasoning is worth keeping in front of whoever builds this: "The instinct to build
inventory here drags in an item pipeline, a screen, and an enum that grows forever, in
service of three numbers." Section 16 has the re-entry condition for real inventory and
this is not it.

Healing is the scarce one. Section 9: the engine has to impose scarcity because the
narrator never will. "The model always says yes. That is not a prompt failure to be
tuned out; it is what a narrator trained to be agreeable does."

use_item is a mechanics-phase tool, not reconcile: a false positive spends a potion the
player still has, which is expensive. Same test as every other tool placement in
AGENTS.md, LLM tools.

Counts fold out of the log like everything else (invariant 8). A new event, not a field
somebody sets.
acceptance_criteria:
Consumable is a closed enum. PartyMember carries a counter map folded from an event.
use_item is in the mechanics tool set, validated server-side, rejected when the count is
zero. The chrome shows counts as text and nothing more. A potion at zero cannot be drunk
however the player phrases it.

title: Prove party state is session-scoped, not room-scoped
description:
Section 9 lists this as the small refactor everything else in the delve depends on:
"Party state is session-scoped, not room-scoped. Today entities are built from room
content, which makes hit points implicitly reset at a room boundary. Rooms should
contribute their occupants and props and nothing else."

M3 appears to have already done most of it. GameEngine.java:73 spawns the party once
at the entrance from entrance.startPositions().party(), and crossExit emits PartyMoved
rather than respawning, so entities survive a crossing in WorldState.entities. That is
a reading of the code, not a measurement.

The job is to prove it and close whatever gap is left, because every other child of
this epic is built on the assumption. Attrition that silently resets at a door is the
whole milestone failing quietly.

Look specifically at: whether anything rebuilds an Entity from RoomDefinition after the
first spawn; whether a room a party returns to re-contributes its occupants (a goblin
left alive in the crypt must be the same goblin, at the same hit points, per the
2026-09-07 playtest); and whether hit points, revealed props and facts all cross
correctly in both directions.
acceptance_criteria:
A test that walks the party across a room boundary and back with damage taken in each
room, asserting hit points, position and revealed state survive both crossings. If any
of it already holds, the test is the deliverable and says so.

title: Turn-1 escalation is a coin flip
description:
Playtest 2026-09-07. Two sessions opened with the identical move — 'I inspect the sarcophagus', failed INVESTIGATION, the first check of the session — and produced two different games.

Session 1 (20260907-030629): spawn_entity only. Five turns of parley followed, and the fight started later when the player chose it.
Session 2 (20260907-195254): spawn_entity AND start_combat in the same response, 4s apart. In initiative before the player had done anything hostile.

dm-tools.md:47 says the situation must change on the SECOND consecutive failure. Both runs escalated on the first failure of the session, and read the same rule opposite ways.

This is the M2 finding 'talking to yourself can start a fight' in a new form, and it is not cosmetic: it decides whether the player gets a negotiation or a fight, on turn one, before they have any information.

The Momentum block only appears when consecutiveFailedChecks > 0 (DmService.java:833), so on the first failure of a session the model sees no momentum line at all and escalates anyway.
acceptance_criteria: A single failed check on turn 1 does not start combat. The two-failure rule holds across repeated runs of the same opening — check it by replaying, not by reading the prompt.
notes: Blocks emberdelve-4h9.5 as of 2026-09-07. Left standalone rather than pulled into M4, but it stops being cosmetic there: an attrition game whose first fight is decided by a coin flip on turn one is unfair in a way the current no-stakes game hides.

title: Play the dungeon and decide whether DIM reads
description:
The gate for this epic. Everything else in it is decided by a fixture; this is
decided by looking.

Must be played in the real Godot client, not headless. AGENTS.md still carries
"Dark neighbour unread" from the M3 gate for exactly this reason — that session
was headless, so whether a room through a doorway reads as a dungeon or as a
hole has never actually been judged.

Follow the M3 gate's shape: cross at least four times, spend real turns in each
room, and rotate the camera (Q/E) through all four corners in both rooms.

WHAT TO LOOK AT

1. The complaint. Does crossing still read as a cut to a new box, or as walking
   into the next part of one place?
2. The crypt's north corners, seen from the gallery, from ALL FOUR camera
   corners. This is the xgg.7 verification and the whole reason the wall rule
   was rewritten. A wall can be right from three corners and wrong from the
   fourth.
3. DIM in both directions, and compare them. The crypt seen from the gallery is
   lit by ambient 0.7; the gallery seen from the crypt by ambient 1.1. That
   drift is predicted and accepted (ADR-0010 era decision, Q9 of the design) —
   the question is whether the darker direction still reads as somewhere you
   have been rather than as a void.
4. Props across a crossing. Reveal the crypt's alcove, cross, look back: still
   there? Reveal the gallery's niche, cross twice: still there? This is
   traversal itself plus the room-qualified PropRef.
5. The camera in the gallery, whose origin is not (0,0). Does the clamp fight
   the follow? Then `debug -> start combat` there: does the framing centre on
   the gallery or snap back toward the crypt?
6. Picking. A click in the DIM room does nothing and swallows no move; the door
   back is still clickable; brazier-east still does not shadow the door.
7. A goblin left behind. Spawn one in the crypt, cross to the gallery, look
   back. The crypt should show no token — ADR-0011's accepted cost. Confirm it
   reads as absence rather than as a bug.
8. The DM, asked about a room it is not in. Type something like "I look back
   through the door at the crypt" and see whether the narration stays coherent
   without the prompt having been widened.
design:
The one decision this session exists to make: DIM or LIT for visited rooms.

That was chosen as DIM in the design grilling with LIT named as the fallback,
and Room.level_for was built to keep the switch to one line. If the darker
direction reads as a void, pull it. If it reads as a room you have been in,
leave it. Either answer closes this ticket; "it was fine" without having looked
at both directions does not.

Two other outcomes ride on this session:

- ADR-0011 is Proposed, not Accepted. It flips to Accepted if item 6 holds in
  play — that is the picking confinement being exercised rather than merely
  compiled.
- If the ambient drift is the problem rather than DIM itself, the second knob is
  a per-room tint, not a change of level. Recorded in the epic's design so the
  fix is not reinvented as "raise the ambient", which AGENTS.md already warns
  against for a different reason.

The session writes itself to server/sessions/. If anything goes wrong, the file
that proves it is already on disk — copy it into docs/evidence/ and it replays
on every build. That is the M2 workflow and it is the reason this ticket does
not need a reproduction script.
acceptance_criteria:
- Four or more crossings played in the real client, camera rotated through all
  four corners in both rooms.
- No hole at the crypt's north corners from any camera corner.
- A written verdict on DIM vs LIT, having looked at both directions, and the
  one-line change made if the verdict is LIT.
- ADR-0011 moved from Proposed to Accepted, or a note saying why not.
- Any fault found is filed with its session file, copied into docs/evidence/ if
  it is worth replaying.
notes:
Item 4 was not actually exercised by the 2026-09-07 sessions. Session 1 revealed zero props. Session 2 revealed the crypt alcove at 20:04:57, after the last crossing at 20:04:24 — so no prop was ever revealed and then crossed away from and returned to. The gallery niche was never found in either run: the player searched the brazier and the pillars, and the revealHint is on the west wall. 'Props survive a crossing' and the room-qualified PropRef are still untested in play.

Everything else on the list was covered, and the epic's DIM question was answered by looking.
close_reason: Played in the real client over two sessions on 2026-09-07. DIM stands — the fallback to LIT is not taken, and the darker direction was judged the better look, inverting the design's expectation that the drift was a cost. ADR-0011 flips to Accepted: picking confinement held in play, and the goblin left behind read as absence rather than as a bug. Findings recorded in AGENTS.md § Judged in play — playtest 2026-09-07. Item 4 (a prop revealed and then crossed away from) was not exercised and is noted there rather than left implied.

title: Draw the shared wall the way coveredWalls() decides it
description:
Rooms.coveredWalls() holds the shared-wall rule server-side, with tests, since emberdelve-5sc: the plane is owned by whichever room is nearer the entrance (ties by roomId), and omission is a 1D interval overlap rather than a direction match. Nothing ships it. RoomView carries no covered-segment field, so room.gd still omits by direction — the room the party is standing in draws the plane, every other room drops the whole run its answering door is in.

Two consequences on screen: the crypt's two 1-unit corner overhangs are missing when seen from the gallery (a hole in a wall is a way out), and with more than two rooms drawn the ownership flips with the party rather than staying put.

Wire it: add the covered segments to RoomView (or a per-room list on SceneState), have GameEngine.scene() fill it from Rooms.coveredWalls(), and have Room._build_walls skip exactly those segments instead of whole runs. Room.build already takes a RoomView and is the one build path for every room, current or not, so this is the last piece.
design: Deliberately left out of emberdelve-xgg.4, which delivered the render levels, the persistent world frame on the client and per-room prop holders. Wiring coveredWalls() is a wire change plus a client rule swap, and it is testable on its own — the synthetic three-room chain in RoomsTest already proves the server half.
acceptance_criteria:
A neighbour drawn beside the current room keeps the part of its perimeter that overhangs the shared run: no hole at the crypt's north corners seen from the gallery.
No two rooms draw stone on the same plane (the seam does not go to noise, and no door grows a second ring handle).
Ownership does not change when the party crosses: the same room draws the same plane from either side.
AGENTS.md's 'decided server-side and not yet drawn' bullet is replaced by what is drawn.
notes: Second hole the whole-run omission leaves, found reviewing emberdelve-xgg.4: with three rooms drawn, a shared plane can be drawn by nobody. omit_shared_wall is now 'every room but the one the party is in', and _on_a_shared_wall drops the run by direction — so in A(current)-B-C, B and C both omit their mutual run and the wall between them is missing entirely. Latent while M3 ships two rooms; live the day a third exists. coveredWalls() already gets this right (exactly one room owns each plane).
close_reason: RoomView.coveredWalls ships Rooms.coveredWalls()' answer and room.gd omits exactly those segments — the crypt's north corners are stone from the gallery, every plane is drawn once by the same room from either side, and the A-B-C plane two neighbours both used to drop is drawn. The doorway is the deliberate exception: a door is one object two rooms address by two ids and World._target_under only scans the current room's walls, so the room the party is in hangs it and every other room leaves its openings open. Room.build takes the current room id rather than a Level so that the agreed DIM-to-LIT fallback cannot hang a second door. Five TDD'd tests, all three client ones mutation-checked against the old direction-match rule. AGENTS.md, ADR-0010 and CONTEXT.md amended. Filed emberdelve-xgg.9 for the generator-era case where a covering room is not on the wire.

title: Record the world-frame decisions and fix the docs they contradict
description:
Written after the server half proves itself, before the client half is wired.

- docs/adr/0009: the world frame is server-owned and anchored at the entrance;
  a shared wall is owned by BFS distance and omitted by geometric overlap;
  visible is not addressable. One ADR, because they are one decision about where
  world-space authority lives.
- CONTEXT.md: add "world frame" and "render level"; correct "scene state", which
  currently reads "the client's whole current picture of a room" and is no longer
  true. Flag any term the code needs that the glossary lacks.
- AGENTS.md's shared-wall bullet is NOT amended here — it goes in emberdelve-5sc,
  in the same commit that makes it false.
design:
Deliberately not written up front. This repo's docs are empirical — AGENTS.md is
wall-to-wall "measured" and "found in play", and ADR-0008 is literally "model
picks come from played sessions". An ADR written before implementation is a
prediction, and the interval-overlap wall rule is the piece most likely to come
back different. Writing it once the synthetic three-room fixture proves the world
frame and the wall rule means it records something demonstrated, while still
landing early enough that the client is built against a written-down rule.

Glossary entries land with the code introducing each term, not in a batch.
acceptance_criteria:
- ADR-0009 exists, follows docs/adr/0000-template.md, and states what was
  rejected (client-side offset accumulation; full world-space packing) and why.
- CONTEXT.md's "scene state" entry is true of the shipped SceneState.
- No rule in AGENTS.md or CONTEXT.md contradicts the code after this epic closes.
close_reason: ADR-0009 (world frame anchored at the entrance), ADR-0010 (the room nearer the entrance owns the shared wall) and ADR-0011 (visible is not addressable, Proposed until the picking confinement is exercised in play) written in 8b3b1eb; index updated and the back-fill note narrowed to 0001-0008. CONTEXT.md in d01a01c: 'scene state' corrected, 'room view', 'world frame' and 'render level' added, Diff's union completed with EntityRemoved and its current-room scoping stated. AGENTS.md needed no further amendment — the shared-wall bullets were already rewritten under 5sc and already flag xgg.7 as the outstanding client half.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
ADRs written 2026-09-06, ahead of the client half as planned. Split into three rather than the one agreed in the grilling: docs/adr/README.md says one decision per file, and origins (a45640f) and wall ownership (03b7dd3) landed as separate commits with separate test classes — you can have entrance-anchored origins and still omit whole runs, which is exactly what a45640f did.

- ADR-0009 the world frame is server-owned and anchored at the entrance (Accepted)
- ADR-0010 the room nearer the entrance owns the shared wall (Accepted)
- ADR-0011 visible is not addressable (Proposed — flips to Accepted when xgg.5 lands the picking confinement)

Index updated; the back-fill note now reads 0001-0008 so it stays true.

STILL OPEN ON THIS TICKET: the CONTEXT.md glossary work. Per the agreed sequencing those terms land with the code that introduces them — 'world frame' and 'render level' plus the corrected 'scene state' entry, which currently reads 'the client's whole current picture of a room' and stops being true at xgg.2.

title: Keep picking and the camera on the room the party is in
description:
Two consequences of the current room no longer sitting at the world origin.

PICKING. world_to_grid still assumes the live room is centred on the origin, so
it silently mis-resolves the moment origins are entrance-anchored. Make it
room-aware — the exact inverse of grid_to_world for a given room — and have
pick_at resolve which room a floor hit landed in. A hit outside the current
room's rectangle returns null: a DIM room is scenery and a click in one must not
issue a move.

_target_under needs no change for this epic. It scans Room/Walls, and the door
back is in the current room's own wall run, so chaining crossings already works.
Neighbour walls live under a different holder and are never scanned, so a DIM
room cannot steal a pick.

CAMERA. Two places assume the origin is the current room's centre:
_framing_target() centres combat framing on Vector3.ZERO, and _clamp_to_room()
builds its clamp corners at +/- extent around the origin. Left alone, standing in
the gallery clamps the camera to a rectangle around the crypt while it tries to
follow a party in the gallery — which is exactly the failure camera_rig.gd:23
warns about, "clamp-to-room quietly cancels the follow". Translate both to the
current room's origin.
design:
Clamp to the current room's rectangle rather than the discovered bounding box.
The bounding box would let the camera drift a long way from the party in a large
dungeon, and _combat_half_height is tuned to fit one room. Adjacent DIM rooms
show up at the frame edges on their own, which is the continuous-dungeon read the
epic is after, without giving up the framing already tuned.

Picks confined to the current room are what hold the "visible is not addressable"
line from the epic's decision 8. Travel to a room two doors away is out of scope
and this is where that stays true rather than half-true.
acceptance_criteria:
- world_to_grid round-trips against grid_to_world for a room at a non-zero origin.
- A click on a DIM room's floor produces no intent and sends nothing.
- The door back is still clickable and still crosses.
- The camera follows the party in a room whose origin is not (0,0), with no
  clamp fighting the follow.
- Combat framing centres on the current room, not the entrance.
notes: Live after emberdelve-xgg.4: the current room now stands at its absolute origin, so World.world_to_grid (world.gd) — still origin-centred — mis-resolves every floor click in any room but the entrance. pick_at drops the click silently, _sync_tokens re-slides tokens on every scene change, and token.gd paths from the wrong square. The branch is playable in the crypt and not in the gallery until this lands. test_world_to_grid_still_inverts_the_current_room asserts the old origin-centred behaviour and needs replacing with a round-trip against a room at a non-zero origin.
close_reason: world_to_grid is room-aware and pick_at resolves the room a floor hit landed in; camera clamp and combat framing translate to the current room's origin. 232 godot tests green, server suite exit 0. Commit c01d33a.

title: Draw visited rooms at a DIM render level
description:
The visual half.

- Give the client one policy function returning a render level per room: BLACK
  (never seen), DIM (visited, not current), LIT (current). Everything else keys
  off that, so switching visited rooms from DIM to LIT is a one-line change.
- DIM builds with real materials and torch models but no OmniLight3D and no
  flames. Only the current room contributes lights.
- The origin table persists across a crossing. World stops clearing _origins and
  _sizes on a roomId change and stops re-centring the new room on the world
  origin; rooms sit where the server put them and the camera moves instead.
- Props get per-room holders. Today Props is flat and keyed by bare prop id, and
  _instance_prop silently returns early when the name is taken. Prop ids are only
  unique within a room (see PropRef): PropPlacer names every room's first pillar
  pillar-0, so drawing two generated rooms would silently drop props. Per-room
  holders fix that and give dimming a natural traversal.
- Room._build_walls' `get_parent() is World` special case goes: every room takes
  its registered origin, including the current one.
design:
DIM as "no lights" rather than "reduced-energy lights" or "tint override" keeps
MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS a per-room budget however large the dungeon gets — only the
current room ever adds lights. Reduced-energy torches would cost 10 omni lights
per visited room and hand the generator milestone a light-count problem on day
one.

Known and accepted: a DIM room's brightness drifts with the current room's
LightingPreset, because the WorldEnvironment ambient is global (TORCHLIT 1.1,
DIM 0.7, DARK 0.35). The crypt seen from the gallery reads darker than the
gallery seen from the crypt. If that reads badly in play, a per-room tint is the
second knob; the first knob is DIM -> LIT.

The prop-id collision is latent today — crypt and gallery ids happen to differ —
and is fixed here rather than deferred because this is the change that makes
multi-room prop rendering exist, and the failure mode is a prop that silently
does not appear. That is the project's characteristic silent failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Crossing to the gallery leaves the crypt drawn at DIM with its props; the scene
  does not re-centre and no room is rebuilt at the world origin.
- Crossing back returns the crypt to LIT and the gallery to DIM, as left.
- A room never entered is still BLACK.
- Only the current room contributes OmniLight3D nodes; count asserted in a test.
- Two rooms carrying the same prop id both draw their prop.
- DIM -> LIT for visited rooms is a one-line change (demonstrated in the commit
  message or a comment naming the line).
close_reason: Render levels landed: Room.level_for is the one policy (LIT current / DIM visited / BLACK never entered), Room.build is the one build path for every room, the client's origin table is never cleared so crossing moves the camera rather than the dungeon, and props hang under Props/<room id> so two rooms sharing a prop id both draw. Godot suite 224 tests green; Java suite 297 green, untouched. Follow-ups filed: emberdelve-xgg.7 (wire Rooms.coveredWalls()), and emberdelve-xgg.5 now depends on this and must land before a non-entrance room is clickable.

title: Read the current room through Table.room() everywhere
description:
Mechanical churn to match the new wire shape. Around fourteen call sites read
room-level fields straight off Table.scene — width, height, floorType, wallType,
lighting, exits, props, roomId — across world.gd, room.gd, camera_rig.gd,
lighting.gd and table.gd. Those fields no longer live at the top level.

Add a Table.room() accessor returning the current room's RoomView, and a
Table.room_by_id() for the others. Convert the call sites. No behaviour change in
this task: the world still draws one lit room and the rest black, exactly as
today, just read through the new shape.

Kept separate from the visual work so that a regression here is obviously churn
and a regression there is obviously the feature.
design:
Table remains the single owner of game state (invariant #3, and CONTEXT.md's
"Table"). The accessor is what stops fourteen call sites each doing their own
lookup into rooms[] by roomId.

Table currently mutates scene["props"] on a PropRevealed diff. That write moves
to the current room's RoomView, which is correct because the diff channel is
current-room-scoped.
acceptance_criteria:
- No production .gd file reads width/height/floorType/wallType/lighting/exits/
  props directly off Table.scene.
- PropRevealed still lands on the current room's props.
- Both suites pass with no visible change to the running game.
close_reason: Table.room()/room_by_id() land; room.gd, camera_rig.gd, lighting.gd and world.gd read the current room through them instead of Table.scene's old flat fields. PropRevealed now writes to the current room's RoomView. Client test suite (scene_fixtures.gd helper + all fixture updates) converted to the new SceneState wire shape. Both suites green: 217/217 Godot GUT, server ./gradlew test.

title: SceneState describes every known room, not one
description:
SceneState carries one room at top level plus a neighbours list of bare outlines.
Reshape it so every room is described the same way:

  SceneState { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities, blocked, mode, combat }

RoomView { roomId, width, height, floorType, wallType, lighting, props, exits,
originX, originZ, visited }. roomId says which room the party is in; entities,
blocked, mode and combat stay session-level and stay scoped to that room.

GameEngine.scene() ships a RoomView for every room in Rooms that the party has
either visited or can see through an exit of the current room. A visited room
carries its visible props, dressed via room(roomId) and filtered by the
room-qualified revealedProps. An unvisited one carries geometry only and
visited=false.

Entities are NOT shipped for non-current rooms. entitiesHere() is unchanged.
design:
Forced by emberdelve-5sc. The shared-wall owner is decided by BFS distance from
the entrance, not by which room the party stands in, so the current room and a
non-current room have to go through the same wall-building code. Two wire shapes
means two code paths and the rule implemented twice — which is how you get a wall
right from one side and wrong from the other.

RoomView matches the EntityView / CombatView naming already in dm.model.

Entities excluded deliberately: a token in a non-current room is a creature the
player can see that the DM's prompt was never told about, which is spec section
8b's contradiction risk with a monster in it. Spec section 4b already keeps
entities in the fold where they were left; this only declines to draw them.

Diff is unchanged. Diff.PropRevealed carries no roomId and does not need one:
reveal_prop only ever offers the current room's hidden props, so the diff channel
stays current-room-scoped by convention. Worth stating rather than rediscovering.

No Event carries SceneState, so SCHEMA_VERSION does not bump and recordFixture is
not required.
acceptance_criteria:
- rooms[] contains the current room, every visited room, and every room visible
  through a current-room exit; nothing else.
- The current room appears in rooms[] in the same shape as every other room.
- A visited room's props include secrets revealed in THAT room and exclude
  secrets revealed elsewhere (PropRef is room-qualified).
- An unvisited room carries visited=false and no props.
- No non-current room carries entities.
- SCHEMA_VERSION unchanged; session-m3-traversal.jsonl replays with exit 0.
close_reason: SceneState reshaped to { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities, blocked, mode, combat }; GameEngine.scene() ships visited + exit-visible rooms uniformly. Java suite (299 tests) and Godot suite (217 tests) pass; session-m3-traversal.jsonl replays identical, exit 0.

title: Anchor every room's origin at the entrance, server-side
description:
RoomOutline.beside computes an offset relative to the room the party is standing
in. That works for one hop and cannot place a room two hops away: composing the
offsets is the client's problem today only because the client never has to.

Walk the exit graph from Rooms.first() breadth-first, composing beside() offsets,
and produce an absolute origin for every room in Rooms. The entrance sits at the
world origin and never moves. beside() itself is unchanged and stays the single
implementation of the door-alignment arithmetic.

Cycles: first path wins. A second path to an already-placed room is ignored, not
reconciled — reconciliation is real world-space packing and belongs to the
generator milestone (spec section 3, "world-space packing").
design:
Chosen over having the client accumulate C_abs = B_abs + offset. RoomOutline's
doc comment states the reason the arithmetic is server-side: "so there is one
implementation of the arithmetic and it can be tested without a renderer."
Client-side accumulation moves composition somewhere it can only be tested with a
renderer, and turns a cycle disagreement into an emergent client behaviour rather
than a defined server one.

A one-way exit already yields null from beside() and is filtered out; a room
reachable only through one is simply not placed and not drawn.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pure function maps Rooms to roomId -> origin, unit-tested with no renderer.
- Rooms.first() is at (0, 0).
- A three-room chain A-B-C places C correctly relative to A.
- A cycle A-B-C-A places every room once, deterministically, first path winning.
- crypt/gallery origins match what RoomOutlineTest already asserts for one hop.
close_reason: Added Rooms.origins(): BFS from first(), composing RoomOutline.beside offsets, into an unmodifiable roomId->RoomOrigin map. TDD'd in RoomsOriginsTest (single room, one-hop matching RoomOutlineTest, three-room chain composition, cycle first-path-wins, one-way-exit exclusion).

title: Visited rooms stay on the board
description:
Today the world shows one room at a time. Crossing a threshold re-centres the
scene on the room just entered and the room just left drops to a near-black
outline, so the dungeon reads as a series of boxes rather than one place.

This epic keeps every room the party has stood in drawn and legible, at a DIM
render level, in a single world frame anchored at the entrance. The party still
occupies exactly one room and can still only act in that room: what changes is
what is drawn, not what is addressable.

Scope is chaining crossings without the scene cutting. Clicking a door two rooms
away and walking there is NOT in scope — that needs multi-room routing the
server does not have and collides with the arrival-narration beat.
design:
Ten decisions, taken in a grilling session on 2026-09-06.

1. RENDER LEVEL. Three levels chosen by one policy function: BLACK (never seen),
   DIM (visited, not current), LIT (current). Making visited rooms LIT instead of
   DIM must stay a one-line change — it is the agreed fallback if DIM looks wrong
   in play.
2. DIM MEANS NO LIGHTS. Real materials, torch models placed, but no OmniLight3D
   and no flames. Only the current room contributes lights, so MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS
   stays a per-room budget however large the dungeon gets. Known consequence: a
   DIM room's brightness drifts with the current room's LightingPreset ambient
   (TORCHLIT 1.1 vs DIM 0.7). Accepted; a per-room tint is the second knob if it
   reads badly.
3. PAYLOAD IS GEOMETRY + PROPS. Visible props including secrets already revealed
   there. No entities — a creature the player can see but the DM was never told
   about is spec section 8b's contradiction problem in a new costume.
4. WORLD FRAME IS SERVER-OWNED, ANCHORED AT THE ENTRANCE. BFS from Rooms.first()
   composing RoomOutline.beside offsets; ship each known room's absolute origin.
   Cycles resolve first-path-wins. Chosen over client-side accumulation because
   RoomOutline's own rationale is that the arithmetic lives server-side "so there
   is one implementation and it can be tested without a renderer". Real
   world-space packing stays deferred to the generator milestone (spec section 3).
5. SHARED WALL OWNERSHIP. The plane is drawn once by whichever room is nearer the
   entrance in that BFS, ties broken by roomId. Omission is a 1D interval overlap
   on the shared plane, not a direction match. This replaces "the room the party
   is standing in owns the shared wall", which stops being a usable rule once more
   than one room is visible.
6. UNIFORM WIRE. SceneState becomes { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities,
   blocked, mode, combat }. Every room including the current one is a RoomView
   carrying origin, size, floorType, wallType, lighting, props, exits, visited.
   Forced by decision 5: the wall owner is decided by BFS distance, not by which
   room the party stands in, so current and non-current rooms must go through one
   code path or the rule gets implemented twice.
7. CAMERA. Clamp and combat framing translate to the current room's origin
   instead of Vector3.ZERO. Not the discovered bounding box — that would let the
   camera drift off the party and _combat_half_height is tuned to one room.
8. DM UNCHANGED. Prompt and ToolSchema stay scoped to the current room. The line
   is: visible is not addressable. This is what keeps out-of-scope travel out
   rather than half-in.
9. FIXTURES ARE SYNTHETIC. Rooms.of() three-room chains and a cycle in the suite;
   no third authored room in content/, so the AGENTS.md anti-goal is untouched.
10. DOCS. One ADR for decisions 4/5/8, written after the server half proves them
    rather than before. AGENTS.md's shared-wall line amended in the same commit
    that makes it false. CONTEXT.md gains "world frame" and "render level" and a
    corrected "scene state" entry, each with the code that introduces the term.

FREE, CONFIRMED: no Event carries SceneState, so SCHEMA_VERSION does not bump,
recordFixture is not needed, and session-m3-traversal.jsonl keeps replaying. Diff
is unchanged and stays current-room-scoped by convention.

RISK: the interval-overlap wall rule is the riskiest piece. It takes on exactly
the parity problem the current code deliberately dodged, and a wall right from
one side and wrong from the other is only visible from one camera corner. Build
it server-side and pure, prove it on the synthetic three-room chain, then wire
the client.
acceptance_criteria:
- Crossing from the crypt to the gallery leaves the crypt drawn, DIM, with its
  props and any secrets revealed there. The scene does not re-centre.
- Crossing back finds the gallery as it was left, and the crypt returns to LIT.
- No hole appears at the crypt's north corners when viewed from the gallery.
- A room never visited is still BLACK and still absent from the DM's prompt.
- Clicking anything in a DIM room does nothing and cannot issue a move.
- Both suites pass; session-m3-traversal.jsonl still replays with exit 0.

title: Props are not click targets yet
description: world.gd _target_under considers only wall segments carrying an exit_id. An earlier cut scanned Props as well, so that objects would be clickable generally, and it broke the door: picking takes the nearest hit, and brazier-east stood between the camera corner and the north wall. It won the ray, had no intent, and fell through to a null square. When a prop gains a real action (open the sarcophagus, search the alcove), add it to _target_under and decide how it ranks against a doorway and against the floor square behind it. test_overlay.gd's DOORWAY fixture now carries the crypt's real furniture, so a regression shows up.
notes: Pulled into M4 (emberdelve-4h9) 2026-09-07. Two children hard-depend on it: 4h9.4 (the objective is a prop you take) and 4h9.6 (DM-placed markers). Section 2a of the design doc is the argument - an objective the player cannot pick up is not an objective, and routing 'take the relic' through free text alone puts a mechanical outcome back on the narrator's side of the governing principle.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text: emberdelve-xgg moves props into per-room holders (prop ids are only unique within a room). When this is picked up, _target_under must scan the current room's holder only — a prop in a DIM room must never win a ray, for the same reason a DIM floor square resolves to no intent.

title: A neighbour room's wall may overhang the shared plane
description: room.gd now has a neighbour omit the entire wall run its answering door is in, so the two rooms do not draw coincident geometry. When the neighbour is WIDER than the room the party is standing in, the part of its perimeter that overhangs the live room's wall is now missing too — its floor runs to an open edge there. Invisible today because a neighbour is painted near-black and the crypt (12) is wider than the gallery (10). Will show the moment the generator packs rooms of mixed sizes. Fix when it does: keep the overhanging segments and drop only the coincident run.
design:
Promoted from latent to live by emberdelve-xgg: the overhang is invisible only
while a non-current room is painted near-black. At the DIM render level it is two
1-unit holes at the crypt's north corners, visible from the gallery. Shipping
that would regress the playtest fix recorded in AGENTS.md — "a hole in the wall
is a way out, and there are no other holes".

The rule "the room the party is standing in owns the shared wall" is also no
longer usable. With several rooms visible at once a middle room has shared walls
on both sides, RoomOutline.back carries only one answering door, and two adjacent
DIM rooms would each omit their shared run and delete the wall between them.

REPLACEMENT RULE, two halves:

1. OWNERSHIP. The shared plane is drawn once, by whichever of the two rooms is
   nearer the entrance in the BFS from emberdelve-xgg.1, ties broken by roomId so
   it is stable and testable.
2. OMISSION. The non-owner omits only the segments the owner geometrically
   covers, computed as a 1D interval overlap on the shared plane using the
   absolute origins. Not a direction match — _on_a_shared_wall's whole-run
   omission is what loses the overhang.

Riskiest piece of the epic. It takes on precisely the parity problem the current
code dodged ("matching segment against segment can half-work when the rooms'
widths differ in parity"), and a wall correct from one side and wrong from the
other is only visible from one camera corner. Absolute server-computed origins
are what make it tractable: the comparison is on known world-space intervals
rather than grid indices of two differently-sized rooms.

Build and prove it server-side and pure, on the synthetic three-room chain,
before any client wiring.

AGENTS.md's shared-wall bullet is amended in the same commit as this change — it
is true until then, and false after.
acceptance_criteria:
- The shared plane between two rooms carries exactly one set of wall segments.
- Crypt (12) viewed from gallery (10): both overhanging north segments present,
  no hole at either corner.
- Two adjacent rooms that are both non-current still have their shared wall.
- A middle room in an A-B-C chain draws correct walls on both shared planes.
- Ownership is deterministic across runs and asserted without a renderer.
- AGENTS.md's "the room the party is standing in owns the shared wall" bullet is
  amended in this commit.
close_reason: Rooms.coveredWalls(): the shared plane is drawn once, by whichever room is fewer doors from the entrance (ties by roomId), and the loser omits only the segments the owner's run contains whole — a 1D interval overlap on absolute origins, not a direction match. Pure and server-side; client wiring is xgg.2/xgg.4. Five TDD'd cases in RoomsCoveredWallsTest, mutation-checked against reversed tiebreak, ignored hop distance, and whole-run omission. AGENTS.md's shared-wall bullet amended.

After a compaction in Claude Code the beads workflow context is gone and nothing restores it, so an agent mid-task can forget to use bd. Add PreCompact and PostCompact entries so context is refreshed the way Codex does it.

description: ADR-0003 currently ends at the M2 split decision and still implies any strong writer is usable in the prose slot. The M2 gate found otherwise: venice-uncensored-role-play was the better voice and the worse follower, so DM_MODEL_PROSE moved to gemini-3-8-flash with DM_REASONING_EFFORT_PROSE=low. Record the amendment and the rule-following bar it establishes for the prose slot.
